_comment: The hand-written half. Edit this daily; fetch-data.mjs merges it with FRED and never overwrites it.
summary: CPI came in hot. Headline 3.7% YoY (3.4% in August, 3.6% expected), core 2.6%. Gas alone was up 9.1% on the month, more than half of the entire headline increase. So inflation is still mostly an oil story. But look at what the bond market did with it. The 10 year spiked to 5.30% on the report, then gave every basis point back and settled at *5.21%*. At the same time the 2 year went up and the 30 year went down. What does this even mean? For weeks the long end has been selling off on its own, no matter what the Fed did. Today that flipped. Hike odds for the 28 Oct meeting jumped from 22% to 50%, and the long end rallied on that. Mixing this all in a pot: the market is pricing a Fed that hikes, and trusting it to work. That is credibility, and the Fed has not had it since it hiked in September. Also, I flagged ISM prices paid at 74 {{since:2026-10-05}}. This print is what that looked like arriving.
_fedPath_note: Every FOMC decision since the last hike, oldest first: the date, the upper bound of the target range after it, and hike / cut / hold. Drawn as the staircase under the Fed and listed in its card. Add a row after each meeting.

news.what: CPI came in hot. Headline 3.7% YoY (3.4% in Aug, 3.6% expected), core 2.6%. Gas +9.1% on the month was over half the headline increase.
Odds of another hike at the 28 Oct meeting jumped to about 50%, from 22% before the report.
ISM services report: PMI 54.9, prices paid 74, the highest since 2022. Activity and spending still high.
Jobs report came out, only 29,000 new jobs added in Sep compared to the estimated 90,000.
Flash PMI released today, composite at 58.4 from 56.0. Economy is running too hot. 10 year is at its highest since 2007.
AI debt is estimated to be $420 billion for 2027, 60% above previous estimates.
UN General Assembly this week. Iran and the Strait of Hormuz are on the agenda.

_news_note: The newspaper on the map. Dated bullets, newest first, five to seven at most; the oldest falls off. Facts only, the take lives in the read. key:true marks one row rust.

_oil_note: Optional daily override. Set asOf to the date you read them and fill wti/brent. Used only while newer than FRED's print - if you stop updating, it falls back to FRED automatically rather than showing an ever-staler number.

notes.10Y: Spiked to 5.30% on the CPI, then gave it back

_curve_note: Optional hand entry for a yield FRED has not published yet. Same rule as oil: only used while newer than FRED. notes/alert are display only. Put alert on whatever the day's story is: it turns the figure rust and is the only thing telling a first-time visitor where to look. strain is the quieter version: a smaller crack on the summit, number stays in ink. track is [open, low, now] for one tenor's day, drawn as a path under the summit; use it only when the path matters more than the close, and leave it out otherwise.
